stories.headline: Tennessee death row inmate survives attempted lethal injection
stories.body: Tennessee prison officials failed to execute death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday night [c1, c8, c15]. The attempted execution took place at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville at about 20:00 local time [c8]. Hours before, the US Supreme Court cleared the way for her execution by lethal injection [c2]. Pike could have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in 200 years [c2]. The scheduled execution procedure involved two injections of pentobarbital [c3]. Two lethal injections failed to kill her [c15]. Her legal team filed an emergency motion after the procedure [c7]. They said Pike lost consciousness, still had a heartbeat, and was audibly snoring [c7]. District Judge Clifton L. Corker issued a ruling [c9]. He said medical personnel began giving medical care to Pike [c9]. Authorities treated Pike at a nearby hospital on October 1 [c1]. Department spokesperson Dorinda Carter said officials followed state execution protocol [c10]. She said they moved Pike to an off-site medical facility [c10]. Dr. Joel Zivot said in an email that Pike will likely suffer a brain injury [c11]. He said this injury will come as a consequence of delayed resuscitation [c11]. Robin M. Maher of the Death Penalty Information Center spoke about execution survivals [c12]. She said no one has stayed alive after receiving lethal injection drugs [c12]. Pike was 18 years old when she killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995 [c4]. She lured Slemmer into woods, cut her throat, and smashed her head with a rock [c16]. Police found a pentagram carved into Slemmer's chest [c5]. Pike's boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp got life in prison with the possibility of parole for his role in the murder [c17].

vocab.meaning: a person living in a prison
the act of bringing someone back to consciousness or life

stories.headline: United States completes full military withdrawal from Iraq
stories.body: United States forces completed their military withdrawal from Iraq on September 30 [c18]. This departure ended a military presence that began with the 2003 invasion [c18]. The final withdrawal followed a 2024 agreement signed between Washington and Baghdad [c19]. US forces left more than two decades after the invasion that overthrew Saddam Hussein [c30]. Iraq declared Sovereignty Day to mark the event [c30]. Iraqis celebrated with night-time events as a four-day national holiday began [c24]. Around 100 British military personnel also departed from Irbil on Wednesday [c25]. British forces left alongside US troops [c25]. The UK Ministry of Defence spoke about military strikes during Operation Inherent Resolve [c29]. It said Royal Air Force aircraft struck more than 2,300 ISIS targets in Iraq [c29]. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi spoke about the end of the coalition mission [c26]. He said Iraq now takes full responsibility for its own security and stability [c26]. US President Donald Trump wrote a message on Truth Social [c27]. He said the exit was a victory for the United States [c27]. He called it a victory for Iraq [c27]. He also called it a decisive victory over ISIS [c27]. A recent UN report assessed the strength of ISIS in Iraq [c28]. The report said counter-terrorism operations left ISIS with several hundred fighters [c28]. It said these fighters are only capable of unsophisticated operations [c28]. More than one million US service members served in Iraq during the first phase of the war [c20]. US troop levels reached about 170,000 personnel during the 2007 surge [c21]. The US Department of Defense recorded 4,419 military deaths during Operation Iraqi Freedom [c22]. It also recorded 31,993 military personnel wounded in action [c22]. Brown University's Costs of War project estimated war spending through early 2023 [c23]. It said the US spent about $1.79 trillion on wars in Iraq and Syria [c23]. Abu Mujahid al-Assaf of Kataib Hezbollah spoke about the departure [c32]. He described the exit as the expulsion of occupation forces [c32]. He said it marks the beginning of full Iraqi sovereignty [c32]. The Iraqi government extended a deadline to negotiate disarming powerful Iran-backed militias [c31]. The new target deadline is June 2027 [c31].

vocab.meaning: full power and independence of a country to govern itself
a group of countries or people working together for a shared purpose

stories.headline: Russia attacks Ukrainian energy grid in massive overnight strike
stories.body: Russia launched a massive combined air strike against Ukraine's energy grid overnight on Wednesday [c33]. The attack killed seven people across five regions [c33]. Ukrainian state grid operator Ukrenergo imposed emergency power cuts in Kyiv and three surrounding regions [c34]. This was the first time Ukrenergo used emergency cuts since spring [c34]. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha spoke about Moscow's actions [c35]. He said Moscow is increasing pressure on civilians as winter approaches [c35]. He said Russia wants to turn cold and darkness into weapons [c35]. Russian strikes damaged the Trypilska thermal power plant [c41]. The plant sits roughly 40 kilometres from Kyiv [c41]. It is the largest supplier of electricity to the capital city [c41]. Kyiv Mayor Vitaly Klitschko said three people died in the capital during the strikes [c42]. He said the dead included a utility company worker at a warehouse building [c42]. Zanny Minton Beddoes of The Economist spoke about the strikes on Kyiv [c40]. She said Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment as Russia tries to make the city unlivable [c40]. A Russian attack drone crashed into a children's playground in Kyiv without exploding [c39].

vocab.meaning: a network of power lines and stations that supplies electricity
a continuous attack with bombs or heavy explosives

stories.headline: Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar stops mid-air attack on Flydubai flight
stories.body: Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar saved a Flydubai flight after his co-pilot attacked him inside the cockpit [c48]. The incident occurred on September 30, 2026, on Flydubai flight FZ1073 [c46, c48]. The plane was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv [c46]. The aircraft transmitted emergency signals during the flight [c46]. It made a sharp descent of more than 17,000 feet from an altitude of 34,000 feet [c46]. The co-pilot stabbed Machchhar inside the cockpit [c48]. Officials said the stabbing was an alleged attempt to crash the plane [c48]. Israeli officials said the co-pilot accused of the attack is an Omani citizen [c57]. Machchhar sustained severe injuries during the assault [c51]. Despite his injuries, he activated the cockpit door release switch [c51]. This action allowed crew members and passengers to intervene [c51]. They stepped in to overpower the attacker [c51]. Passenger Yaniv Hayoun said he placed the attacker in a chokehold [c58]. He said he dragged the attacker out after catching him attempting to destroy instrument panels [c58]. Two off-duty Flydubai pilots travelling as passengers also stepped in [c52]. They assisted in overpowering the attacker [c52]. They also helped in diverting the aircraft [c52]. The plane diverted to Prince Sultan Bin Abdel Aziz Airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia [c47]. It was carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children [c47]. The Israeli embassy in Australia confirmed that a Jewish couple from Sydney was on board [c59]. Israel's ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman spoke about the attack [c60]. He said it was an attempt to hit at peace established by the Abraham Accords [c60]. Flydubai temporarily suspended flights to and from Israel following the attack [c45]. Machchhar is a 50-year-old native of Mumbai [c53]. He spent 11 years with SpiceJet before joining Flydubai in 2022 [c53]. Machchhar logged nearly 9,750 flying hours over a 15-year career [c54]. He primarily flew Boeing 737 aircraft [c54]. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Machchhar a hero [c49]. He said India is proud of him [c49]. President Droupadi Murmu commended Machchhar on X for his bravery and quick response [c50]. Airline SpiceJet praised Machchhar and said all of India is proud [c56]. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also called Machchhar a true hero [c55].

vocab.meaning: to turn or cause to turn from one course to another

stories.headline: INDIA opposition bloc launches nationwide protests over Election Commission voter drive
stories.body: Leaders from 19 opposition parties in the INDIA bloc called for future elections in India to use paper ballots [c72]. The opposition bloc announced a series of nationwide protest actions [c66]. They announced a Save Democracy March from October 2 to October 8 [c66]. They also planned a protest march to the Election Commission on October 6 [c66]. They scheduled a meeting with President Droupadi Murmu [c66]. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi questioned changes made to the online Form 6 voter registration form [c61]. He asked who at the Election Commission ordered Tata Consultancy Services to alter the form on the ECINET portal [c61]. Tata Consultancy Services handles core digital backend infrastructure for the Election Commission [c62]. An investigative report by The Indian Express revealed details about internal objections [c63]. The report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to changes on the portal [c63]. Former Chief Election Commissioner O. P. Rawat said the Election Commission has lost credibility [c71]. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh cited Rawat as saying nearly 14 crore voters lost their voting rights through the Special Intensive Revision [c70]. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that the voter drive was a backdoor National Register of Citizens [c75].

vocab.meaning: basic physical and organizational structures needed for an operation
the quality of being trusted and believed in
